name: Illinois

context: IL 340: Cover crops reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion; the standard says to time establishment so soil is protected during critical erosion periods.
IL 345: For wind erosion, determine the required height of standing residue after harvest and how long it must be kept, plus row direction and ridge height.
cover_rules: IL 340: Seed a minimum of 3 species of plants that includes 2 or 3 plant families to provide diverse soil benefits.
IL 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and terminate as late as practical to maximize plant biomass.
residue: IL 329: Use current wind erosion prediction technology to set the randomly distributed surface residue needed, time of year it must be present, and surface soil disturbance allowed.
IL 345: Select tillage equipment that leaves enough aboveground residue during periods with the highest erosion rates; crop interval STIR value must be no greater than 80.
barriers: IL 603: Herbaceous wind barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent during critical wind erosion periods.
IL 603: Barrier spacing must not exceed 10 times the planned barrier height; orient barriers perpendicular to the prevailing wind.
windbreak: IL 380: The protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side; orient windbreaks perpendicular to the wind and choose species taller than the crop.

seedWin.text: IL 342: Oats may be used for seedings planted early spring to August 15.
IL 342: Wheat, Cereal Rye, or Triticale must be used for seedings planted after August 15.
